```{julia}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
import Pkg
Pkg.activate(@__DIR__)                      # the isolated report/ project (CairoMakie)
using CairoMakie, DelimitedFiles, Printf
CairoMakie.activate!(type = "png", px_per_unit = 2)

const DATADIR = normpath(joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "..", "output", "validation"))

# read a marginals CSV -> Dict (tag, rank, copy) => Vector{(x, density)}
function load_marginals(path)
    raw, _ = readdlm(path, ','; header = true)
    d = Dict{Tuple{String,Int,Int}, Vector{Tuple{Float64,Float64}}}()
    for i in axes(raw, 1)
        key = (String(raw[i, 1]), Int(raw[i, 2]), Int(raw[i, 3]))
        push!(get!(d, key, Tuple{Float64,Float64}[]), (Float64(raw[i, 4]), Float64(raw[i, 5])))
    end
    for v in values(d); sort!(v); end
    return d
end

grid = load_marginals(joinpath(DATADIR, "grid_marginals.csv"))
ct   = load_marginals(joinpath(DATADIR, "ct_marginals.csv"))

# accent colors: teal = flat base (t=0), amber = sharp target (t=1)
const HUE = Dict("t0.000000" => colorant"#0e7c72", "t1.000000" => colorant"#b3630a")
const ROW = [("t0.000000", "t = 0  ·  flat base"), ("t1.000000", "t = 1  ·  sharp target")]

# overlay small-multiples: rows = the two endpoints, cols = district ranks
function overlay(data, ranks; title = "")
    fig = Figure(size = (200 * length(ranks) + 90, 460))
    for (ri, (tag, rowlab)) in enumerate(ROW)
        base = HUE[tag]
        soft = RGBAf(base.r, base.g, base.b, 0.32)
        for (ci, rank) in enumerate(ranks)
            ax = Axis(fig[ri, ci];
                      title = ri == 1 ? "Rank $rank" : "",
                      titlesize = 13,
                      ylabel = ci == 1 ? rowlab : "",
                      ylabelsize = 12, ylabelcolor = base,
                      xticklabelsize = 9, yticksvisible = false,
                      yticklabelsvisible = false, xgridvisible = false)
            copies = sort([c for (t, r, c) in keys(data) if t == tag && r == rank])
            n = length(copies)
            meanx = nothing; meany = nothing
            for c in copies
                pts = data[(tag, rank, c)]
                xs = first.(pts); ys = last.(pts)
                lines!(ax, xs, ys; color = soft, linewidth = 1.1)
                if meany === nothing
                    meanx = xs; meany = copy(ys)
                else
                    meany .+= ys
                end
            end
            meany ./= n
            lines!(ax, meanx, meany; color = base, linewidth = 2.2)
        end
    end
    Label(fig[0, :], title; fontsize = 15, font = :bold, padding = (0, 0, 6, 0))
    rowgap!(fig.layout, 10); colgap!(fig.layout, 10)
    fig
end
nothing
```

## Question

For the **standard cycle walk** (Metropolis–Hastings on the fixed target, *not* AIS), how sharp
can the target measure get before independent chains stop agreeing? We probe along the line
**γ = t, iso = 0.3·t**, $t \in [0,1]$, from a flat base ($t=0$) to a sharp target ($t=1$).

At each point we run **8 independent copies** (distinct seeds), **20,000 samples** each, spacing
1000 MH steps, and compare the **rank-ordered marginals of the per-district log spanning-tree
count** (`get_log_spanning_trees`, sorted ascending per plan).

**Verdict rule.** CONVERGED iff, for *every* district rank, the max pairwise total-variation
distance between the 8 copies' binned marginals stays within the split-half noise floor,
$\text{maxTV} \le 2\,\text{noise} + 0.02$. Bisection tests the endpoints first (expecting $t=0$
CONVERGED, $t=1$ NOT), then bisects to bracket the break.

## Headline result

**The bisection never triggered — the cycle walk converges across the entire line on both
graphs.** Both endpoints came back CONVERGED, so there is no critical $t^\*$ to bracket in
$[0,1]$; the driver's STRICT guard stopped before bisecting.

| Case | $t=0$ | $t=1$ | transition |
|------|:-----:|:-----:|:----------:|
| Grid (10×10, 3 dist) | CONVERGED | CONVERGED | none |
| CT (5 dist)          | CONVERGED | CONVERGED | none |

All 8 CT copies at $t=1$ completed the full 20,004 lines — the result is real, not an artifact of
the overnight hamilton storage outage (see Notes).

## Grid (10×10, 3 districts)

```{julia}
#| label: fig-grid
#| fig-cap: "Grid: rank-ordered log-spanning-tree marginals, 8 copies overlaid (translucent) with the pointwise mean (solid). Top row t=0, bottom row t=1. A single tight band = the chains agree."
overlay(grid, [1, 2, 3]; title = "Grid — 8 independent copies per panel")
```

The grid is essentially flat from base to sharp target — the copy-mean spread is ≈ 0.03–0.05 nats
at both ends. The 3-district / 100-node graph is too small to strain the sampler anywhere.

Verdict stats (`maxTV` = between-copy TV; `2·noise` = pass threshold; `meanΔ` = copy-mean spread,
nats):

| point | rank | maxTV | 2·noise | maxKS | meanΔ |
|:-----:|:----:|------:|--------:|------:|------:|
| t=0 | 1 | 0.0207 | 0.0549 | 0.0166 | 0.054 |
| t=0 | 2 | 0.0184 | 0.0545 | 0.0144 | 0.047 |
| t=0 | 3 | 0.0234 | 0.0533 | 0.0160 | 0.028 |
| t=1 | 1 | 0.0191 | 0.0667 | 0.0114 | 0.035 |
| t=1 | 2 | 0.0165 | 0.0503 | 0.0141 | 0.028 |
| t=1 | 3 | 0.0202 | 0.0601 | 0.0141 | 0.023 |

## CT (5 districts)

```{julia}
#| label: fig-ct
#| fig-cap: "Connecticut: same overlay, 5 district ranks. The t=0 row is a single tight band; in the t=1 row the bands widen and the copies begin to pull apart — the sampler is straining at the sharp target, though still within its own noise floor."
overlay(ct, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; title = "CT — 8 independent copies per panel")
```

CT passes the verdict at both ends, but the mixing clearly gets harder as $t \to 1$:

| point | rank | maxTV | 2·noise | maxKS | meanΔ |
|:-----:|:----:|------:|--------:|------:|------:|
| t=0 | 1 | 0.0219 | 0.0557 | 0.0151 | 0.174 |
| t=0 | 3 | 0.0243 | 0.0657 | 0.0133 | 0.131 |
| t=0 | 5 | 0.0235 | 0.0703 | 0.0197 | 0.333 |
| t=1 | 1 | 0.1602 | 0.5367 | 0.1615 | **2.66** |
| t=1 | 2 | 0.1713 | 0.4619 | 0.1726 | **2.19** |
| t=1 | 3 | 0.1512 | 0.3722 | 0.1534 | **1.78** |
| t=1 | 4 | 0.1090 | 0.2246 | 0.1094 | **1.37** |
| t=1 | 5 | 0.0726 | 0.1619 | 0.0739 | **1.26** |

| CT metric (max over ranks) | $t=0$ | $t=1$ | change |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| between-copy meanΔ (nats)   | ~0.1–0.3 | 1.3–2.7 | **~10–20×** |
| within-chain floor 2·noise  | ~0.06    | 0.16–0.54 | **~10×** |
| between-copy maxTV          | ~0.02    | 0.07–0.17 | ~7× |

Because the verdict is **relative** (between-copy TV vs the chain's own split-half noise), the gate
gets *easier to pass* exactly as mixing worsens — which is why CT $t=1$ reads CONVERGED despite a
2.7-nat mean spread.

## Interpretation

The **AIS weight collapse observed earlier was an importance-weighting / annealing-schedule
problem, not a failure of the underlying cycle walk to mix.** As a direct sampler at the fixed
target, the walk stays self-consistent across independent runs over the whole (γ, iso) line, on
both graphs. The graceful CT slow-down marks where a harder case (NC, 14 districts) or a longer run
would push it past breaking.

## Next steps

1. **Define the break we want.** The current gate is relative. If the interest is *mixing rate*,
   switch to an **absolute** criterion (fixed ESS or fixed TV tolerance) — that would flip CT $t=1$
   to a fail and give the bisection an actual $t^\*$ to bracket.
2. **Run NC (14 districts).** The true stress case, where AIS collapsed hardest. The rig is ready:
   `CASE=nc bash validation/hpc/run_bisection_study.sh`.
3. **Sample budget.** The CT $t=1$ slow-down is visible but sub-floor at 20k; a longer run would
   resolve whether the copies genuinely agree or eventually separate.

## Notes

- **hamilton storage outage.** During the CT run the home/NFS filesystem hung for ~3 hours
  (07-11 ~23:10 → 07-12 ~10:29). Network stayed healthy; the chains blocked in I/O wait and resumed
  on recovery, inflating CT $t=1$ wall-time (2290 s vs a nominal ~9 min). Sample counts are
  complete, so results are unaffected.
- **Reproduce.** `JULIA="julia +1.12.6" THREADS=60 CASE=ct bash validation/hpc/run_bisection_study.sh`
  on hamilton; then `dump_marginals.jl --case ct --tags t0.000000,t1.000000` produces the CSVs this
  report reads. Per-point verdict logs and `bisection_<case>_summary.tsv` land in
  `validation/hpc/logs/`.
